chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from the one who narrated to him, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not ask my community in their gatherings, so you would make them miserly.'

key_terms.فَتُبَخِّلُوهَا: so you would make them miserly

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette regarding asking people for favors in gatherings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet's concern for the psychological burden of repeated requests on the community, warning that excessive asking can lead to stinginess (bukhl) rather than generosity. It underscores the Islamic etiquette of moderation in seeking help and respecting the social dynamics of communal gatherings. The narration reflects the broader Shia emphasis on maintaining social harmony and preventing the depletion of others' willingness to give.
